classification.difficultyReason: Recover the projection components and angle, then calculate maximum height and speeds at two times.

content.prompt: A particle is projected upwards at $10\text{ m s}^{-1}$. The horizontal component of velocity is $6\text{ m s}^{-1}$. Find:

children.label: a
children.prompt: the initial vertical component of velocity,

answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}\dot y(0)&=\sqrt{10^2-6^2}\\&=\sqrt{100-36}\\&=8\text{ m s}^{-1}\end{aligned}$$

The vertical component is upwards.

children.label: b
children.prompt: the angle of projection, to the nearest degree,

answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}\theta&=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac86\right)\\&=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac43\right)\\&\approx53^\circ\end{aligned}$$

The angle is above the horizontal.

children.label: c
children.prompt: the maximum height above the launch point (use $g=10\text{ m s}^{-2}$),

answer.worked:
At maximum height, $\dot y(t)=0$.

$$\begin{aligned}0&=8-10t\\t&=0.8\text{ s}\\y(0.8)&=-5(0.8)^2+8(0.8)\\&=3.2\text{ m}\end{aligned}$$

children.label: d
children.prompt: the speed after the following times, assuming the particle remains in flight. Give answers to 1 decimal place. Use $g=10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

answer.worked:
$\dot x=6\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

$$\begin{aligned}\dot y(2)&=8-10(2)\\&=-12\text{ m s}^{-1}\\\text{Speed}&=\sqrt{6^2+(-12)^2}\\&=6\sqrt5\text{ m s}^{-1}\\&\approx13.4\text{ m s}^{-1}\end{aligned}$$

$\dot x=6\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

$$\begin{aligned}\dot y(3.1)&=8-10(3.1)\\&=-23\text{ m s}^{-1}\\\text{Speed}&=\sqrt{6^2+(-23)^2}\\&=\sqrt{565}\text{ m s}^{-1}\\&\approx23.8\text{ m s}^{-1}\end{aligned}$$
